Promote AEHR to the underfollowed lane for later Layer 2 validation: possible chokepoint in wafer-level burn-in/test for AI processors, silicon photonics, high-power semiconductors, and known-good-die flows.

This pass did not expand mask inspection, probe cards, formal EDA verification, thermal/mechanical simulation, or advanced-packaging inspection specialists; later passes should search Camtek, FormFactor, Onto Innovation, Nova, Synopsys, Cadence, Keysight, Teradyne, and simulation/software names separately.
ONTO should remain in the Layer 1 universe for the advanced-packaging metrology/inspection/process-control subnode; evidence strength is above average but requires revenue-mix validation.
FORM should remain in the Layer 1 universe for wafer-level test, probe cards, and known-good-die economics tied to chiplets, HBM, and advanced packaging.
PDFS is a lower-attention EDA-adjacent/yield-control software hypothesis; it needs proof that advanced-node or advanced-packaging complexity is translating into durable revenue growth.

Reference leaders ASML and KLA should be kept as context anchors, but future passes should avoid overfilling the list with mega-cap equipment names and instead test smaller niches such as mask inspection, e-beam review, reticle handling, probe-card materials, socket/test interfaces, and fab analytics.

FORM should remain in the semi equipment / process-control universe as an underfollowed advanced-packaging wafer-test and probe-card candidate; next layer should verify HBM / advanced-package revenue mix and customer concentration.

PDFS should remain in the EDA-adjacent / yield-control software universe as a low-attention semiconductor manufacturing analytics and factory-connectivity candidate; next layer should verify AI / advanced-packaging exposure and recurring revenue quality.

AEHR should be tracked as a speculative-shadow test-equipment candidate tied to wafer-level burn-in for AI processors, silicon photonics, and optical I/O; survival depends on evidence of repeat production orders and reduced SiC customer concentration.

Within the broader ASML / KLA / Applied Materials reference-equipment universe, the under-mapped subnodes for Layer 2 appear to be: advanced probe cards, known-good-die test, wafer-level burn-in, semiconductor factory data connectivity, and yield analytics.

Need a follow-up pass on non-US but US-traded metrology / inspection candidates such as Camtek and Nova, plus US-listed reference names such as KLA and Onto Innovation, to compare purity, valuation pressure, and actual AI / advanced-packaging exposure.
Add ONTO as an advanced-packaging process-control and metrology/inspection candidate; treat as large-cap but still useful for second-order mapping versus ASML/KLA.
Add FORM as a wafer-level test/probe-card chokepoint candidate tied to advanced packaging, HBM, and AI accelerator production-test complexity.
Add PDFS as an underfollowed EDA-adjacent yield-analytics and semiconductor data-infrastructure candidate; survival in later layers depends on proof of advanced-node/advanced-packaging/HBM adoption.
Still need a later pass for mask inspection, e-beam inspection, reticle inspection, substrate inspection, thermal/mechanical simulation, and non-US listed niche suppliers with ADRs or OTC access.
